I'm translating a Jags program concerning elastic net in probit regression into Stan language.

The background is the probit regression with hierarchical priors on hyperparameters:

likelihood : Y | beta0,beta,x,sigma is a "function"(likelihood)  L(y;g(beta0+beta*x),sigma)

a1 ~exponential(mu1);

a2~ exponential(mu2);

beta0~normal(0,sd_b0);

hierarchical formulation:

tau~ gamma (shape,scaleg) T[1,];

beta~ normal(0.0,sqrt((tau[j]-1)/(tau[j]*a2)));

scalet<-pow(a1,2)/(8*a2);

parts:
I couldn't parse that all out into a question.
Was there a syntax error you're still dealing with?

The information messages aren't errors --- just issues with
floating point arithmetic that usually resolve themselves during
warmup if the model's well formulated.

The problem you're having is likely this:
> beta~ normal(0.0,sqrt((tau[j]-1)/(tau[j]*a2)));

Because you don't constrain tau in any way. You need
to make sure a2 > 0 and tau > 1 for this to make sense,
but you have left them unconstrained:

> parameters{
>
> real beta0;
>
> vector[p] beta;
>
> vector[p] tau;
>
> real a1;
>
> real a2;

You need to declare with constraints:

vector<lower=1>[p] tau;
vector<lower=0> a1;

There may be other problems, but you need to take care of this first.

- Bob

The information messages aren't errors --- just issues with
floating point arithmetic that usually resolve themselves during
warmup if the model's well formulated.

The problem you're having is likely this:

> beta~ normal(0.0,sqrt((tau[j]-1)/(tau[j]*a2)));

Because you don't constrain tau in any way.  You need
to make sure a2 > 0 and tau > 1 for this to make sense,
but you have left them unconstrained:

> parameters{

>                                                real beta0;
>
>                                                vector[p] beta;

>
>                                                real a1;
>
>                                                real a2;

You need to declare with constraints:

  vector<lower=1>[p] tau;
  vector<lower=0> a1;

There may be other problems, but you need to take care of this first.

- Bob

> On Jan 15, 2015, at 3:29 PM, Luke Itiny <luke...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> Thank you very much, Bob!!
>
> I forgot those constraints.
> I've corrected my code but I have the same type of warning(at bottom).
> Should I regard these informational messages as a wrong formulation of the model?

No, it usually just means that the step size is too large when following
the gradient. Stan adapts step size and mass matrix during warmup.
Too small a step means things go too slowly and too large a step means
these kinds of errors and Metropolis rejections, so we try to find the
middle ground.

If you only get a few of these during warmup, it's OK. If they
persist, there's a problem with the model.

You can try lowering initial step size, which often causes them to
go away.
> It's quite an easy model, but I cannot find the causes for these warning :(

It's probably in the standard deviation being able to be very tiny.
Where is it at when Stan's done sampling? Does n_eff look OK?

- Bob
